Of the four divergences this rollup carried, G1 is CLOSED -- glass_eye.py:43-59 now takes the per-card `run.player_rng.rewards.next_float()` upgrade roll before the is_upgradable test, so the screens spend 15 NextItem + 15 NextFloat on PlayerRng.Rewards as CardFactory.CreateForReward does -- and G2 is closed on the parity path (see that guard for the legacy-branch residue). guards.what: G2 (LIVE): the port's docstring claims the options are 'never upgraded'; the game's upgrade odds are `act_index * UpgradedCardOddScaling` for every non-Rare, i.e. non-zero from act 1 on
guards.issue: NARROWED 2026-07-27, and the residue is scope-dependent -- say so rather than clear it. THE PARITY PATH IS FIXED: sts2_rl/relics/glass_eye.py:43-59 now draws `run.player_rng.rewards.next_float()` per created card and applies `odds = run.act_index * UPGRADED_CARD_ODD_SCALING` to every non-Rare, which is CardFactory.RollForUpgrade (CardFactory.cs:288-304) with the 0.25 non-ascension scaling the sim already pins, and the docstring no longer claims the options are 'never upgraded'. WHAT REMAINS: the LEGACY (non-parity) branch at glass_eye.py:60-61 is still `[make_card(cid) for cid in run.rng.sample(matching, count)]` with NO upgrade roll at all, where the sim's own house convention -- rewards.create_reward_cards (sts2_rl/rewards.py:296-302) -- performs the roll in BOTH modes and varies only the STREAM. So on the RL path Glass Eye's non-Rare options are never upgraded, where the game upgrades them with probability act_index x 0.25. Left as a gap rather than cleared because whether the legacy branch is in audit scope is a contract question this entry cannot settle.

guards.what: G3 (LIVE): CardFactory fires `Hook.TryModifyCardRewardOptions` (BOTH phases) at the end of every CreateForReward; the sim's glass_eye never dispatches modify_card_reward_options
guards.issue: MECHANISM: CardFactory.cs:104 runs `if (!options.Flags.HasFlag(CardCreationFlags.NoModifyHooks) && Hook.TryModifyCardRewardOptions(...))`, and Hook.TryModifyCardRewardOptions (Hook.cs:1445-1468) walks every listener's TryModifyCardRewardOptions and then every listener's TryModifyCardRewardOptionsLate. GlassEye sets only NoRarityModification, so the hooks DO run on its five screens. glass_eye.py:30-48 builds the options with make_card and hands them straight to run.select_cards -- the sim's own dispatch site for this hook (rewards.py:298-301) is bypassed. REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed -- `py audit/tools/relic_probes_b06.py glass-eye`): with relic/glitter in the run (Ancient, granted by the ported Nonupeipe shrine, and its port DOES implement modify_card_reward_options), Glass Eye's five granted cards come out as [breakthrough None, breakthrough None, pillage None, evil_eye None, barricade None) -- not one Glam, where the game Glams every eligible option. The same silence applies to the three egg relics (an offered Power would arrive un-upgraded with Frozen Egg in the run), to Silver Crucible, Silken Tress and Fresnel Lens. Note the fix is one call, but it must run BEFORE the options are shown, not after the pick.

guards.what: G4 (LIVE): the candidate pool is `pool_card_ids()` (FilterForCombat) where a reward draws from `GetUnlockedCards`, so Feed and Not Yet can never be offered
guards.issue: MECHANISM: GlassEye.cs:29 builds `CardCreationOptions.ForNonCombatWithUniformOdds(new [Owner.Character.CardPool], c => c.Rarity == rarity)`, and CreateForReward resolves the candidates through `options.GetPossibleCards(player)` minus the blacklist, then (Uniform branch) excludes only Basic and Ancient rarity (CardFactory.cs:216-225) -- the combat-only filter never applies to rewards. glass_eye.py:22, 24 imports and calls `pool_card_ids()`, whose docstring says it mirrors FilterForCombat and drops `can_be_generated_in_combat=False` cards (cards/pool.py:100-117). The sim HAS the right helper: `reward_pool_card_ids()` (cards/pool.py:120-133) exists for exactly this and its docstring names Feed and NotYet as the affected cards. REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed -- `py audit/tools/relic_probes_b06.py glass-eye`): the reward-eligible ids pool_card_ids() drops are exactly [feed RARE, not_yet RARE], and Glass Eye's fifth screen is the Rare screen, so two Rare cards are permanently absent from it. This is the same mistake the project already fixed once elsewhere -- the batch-16 conformance finding 'reward pool = full GetUnlockedCards, not FilterForCombat (Feed/NotYet offerable)' -- and it changes both which cards appear and, because the candidate list is shorter, which index each NextItem draw lands on.

guards.what: G5 (DORMANT): C# populates ALL FIVE rewards before offering any of them; the sim populates, resolves and ADDS one screen at a time
guards.issue: MECHANISM: RewardsCmd.OfferCustom -> RewardsSet.Offer -> GenerateWithoutOffering loops `foreach (Reward reward in Rewards) reward.Populate()` and only then offers (RewardsSet.cs:125-147, 153-159). So all 15 cards exist before the player picks anything. glass_eye.py:29-50 loops the five rarities and calls `run.add_card` inside the loop, so screen N+1's options are created after screen N's pick has already joined the deck. DORMANT: the observable requires a listener whose card creation depends on deck contents, and the sim's card-creation path consults the pool and the rarity only -- the deck-reading hooks (after_card_added_to_deck, used by relics/book_of_five_rings.py and lucky_fysh.py) change max HP and gold rather than the pool. Porting a relic or effect whose card-reward options depend on the deck (a 'no duplicates of cards you own' filter is the obvious shape) makes it live, as does implementing G3 with a relic whose reward hook counts deck cards. Also note the interleave costs nothing in draw ORDER today, because each screen's draws are contiguous on the same stream in both orders.

guards.what: N1 (SETTLED BY EXECUTION): the reward blacklist resets per SCREEN, so the same card can be offered on two screens of the same rarity
guards.rationale: Binding rule 5: the port's comment asserts 'the reward blacklist accumulates within each rarity's screen' and that had to be checked. CardFactory.CreateForReward declares `List<CardModel> list = new List<CardModel>()` LOCALLY per call (CardFactory.cs:91) and passes it as the blacklist for each of that call's cardCount picks, so it is per-CardReward and not per-RewardsSet. glass_eye.py:40-45 rebuilds `bl = list(matching)` per rarity and removes each pick from it, which is the same scope. Executed (`py audit/tools/relic_probes_b06.py glass-eye`): the five cards granted include `breakthrough` TWICE -- once from each Common screen -- which is exactly what a per-screen blacklist permits and a per-set blacklist would forbid.

guards.what: N2: `RewardsCmd.OfferCustom` is a take-or-skip screen set; the port takes `run.select_cards('card_reward', options, 1)` and adds whatever comes back
guards.rationale: Each of the five CardRewards is individually skippable in the game. glass_eye.py:49-50 iterates whatever select_cards returns and adds it, so a policy that returns [] declines that screen -- the sim's choice seam is present and honoured. Same verdict and same reasoning as audit/records/relic/calling_bell.json G3 (the divergent thing is the sim's player-choice model, applied consistently across reward offers), binding rule 3. Recorded so a fixer does not turn the loop into an unconditional grant.

guards.rationale: GlassEye.cs has no `HasUponPickupEffect => true` override and glass_eye.py sets no has_upon_pickup_effect, so the two agree -- checked because the sibling upon-pickup relics in this batch (fragrant_mushroom, gnarled_hammer, golden_compass) all DO declare it and a missing declaration is exactly the defect batch 3 recorded for relic/byrdpip. guards.what: N4: the five rarities and their ORDER -- Common, Common, Uncommon, Uncommon, Rare -- and 3 options per screen
guards.rationale: GlassEye.cs:18-31 builds the array in that order and passes `new CardReward(options, 3, Owner)`; glass_eye.py:25-29 iterates the same five values in the same order with CHOICES = 3 (glass_eye.py:17). Order is load-bearing because all five screens draw from one Rewards stream. No AscensionHelper branch in GlassEye.cs, so 3 and the rarity list are the non-ascension values.

guards.what: N5: `count = min(self.CHOICES, len(matching))` and `if count == 0: continue` (glass_eye.py:33-35) vs C#, which throws when a rarity has no candidates
guards.rationale: CardFactory.CreateForReward raises InvalidOperationException when NextItem returns null (CardFactory.cs:237-240); the sim skips the screen instead. Same reachable behaviour: the Ironclad pool has at least 3 cards at every one of the three rarities, so neither branch is taken. Recorded because the sim's tolerance would hide a pool-shrinking bug that C# would crash on.
